$comment: High contrast (§5.20) — accessibility, not decoration.
DATA, not code: this file is the proof that a theme is a token map. Nothing
in src/ knows these values; the applier sets whatever names appear here that
theme/tokens.ts lists as themeable.
Built on the nordic preset, so anything omitted falls back to a dark value —
but it deliberately omits nothing (tokens.drift.test.ts enforces that): a
contrast theme that inherits half its palette is a contrast theme by luck.
Structure comes from BORDERS, not from surface tints — surfaces are near
black and the frames are bright, which is how a high-contrast UI stays
readable when surface differences are the first thing a low-vision user
loses. The lifts are transparent for the same reason: a shadow you cannot
see is a boundary you cannot see. They are '0 0 #0000' and NOT 'none',
because a shadow token is concatenated into a shorthand list at some call
sites and 'none' would make the whole declaration invalid — see the note in
theme/tokens.ts.
Ratios are asserted in tokens.drift.test.ts — body text >= 7:1 (WCAG AAA),
secondary text >= 4.5:1, structural edges >= 3:1. Change a value here and
the test tells you if it still qualifies. Words written ON a status fill
(the preflight banner) are held to 4.5:1 in EVERY theme, this one included.
KNOWN GAP: those pairs are ink-on-surface. Surface-vs-surface separation is
NOT audited, and a theme cannot reach the derived layer-3 tokens at all —
so the selected-row tint and the auto-group surface are nearly invisible
here. Neither hides information (the row keeps its accent stripe, an auto
group keeps its ink), but they are decoration in this theme rather than a
signal.
